wikipedia.title: Mysore Zoo
wikipedia.text: Mysore Zoo (or Mysuru Zoo), officially known as Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Gardens, is a composite of zoological gardens and animal park located in the southern Indian city of Mysore, Karnataka. Stretching across a 157-acre (64 ha)-expanse and situated at about 700 metres (0.43 miles) from Mysore Palace, it is the oldest zoo in India and one of the oldest in the world. One of the most popular zoos in India and one of the city's most popular attractions, it is home to a wide range of over 168 species.

wikipedia.title: Chamarajendra Academy of Visual Arts
wikipedia.text: Chamarajendra Academy of Visual Arts (CAVA) is a visual art school in Mysore, in the state of Karnataka in India. The academy is affiliated to the University of Mysore and offers courses in drawing, painting, sculpture, graphics, applied arts, photography and photo-journalism and art history. CAVA awards degrees in Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) and Master of Fine Arts (MFA).

wikipedia.title: Regional Museum of Natural History Mysore
wikipedia.text: The Regional Museum of Natural History at Mysore is a museum in India with exhibits on plants, animals and geology of the southern region of India. Established in 1995, it is located on the banks of Karanji Lake.

wikipedia.title: Defence Food Research Laboratory
wikipedia.text: The Defence Food Research Laboratory (DFRL) is an Indian defence laboratory of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO). Located in Mysore, Karnataka, it conducts research and development of technologies and products in the area of food science and technology to cater the varied food challenges for the Indian Armed Forces. DFRL is organised under the Life Sciences Directorate of DRDO. The present director of DFRL is Dr. A D Semwal.

wikipedia.title: Mysore City lakes
wikipedia.text:
Mysore, Karnataka, has major five lakes, some of which are under restoration with funds provided by the Asian Development Bank and government of Karnataka. These lakes are:

Dalavai Lake
Devanoor Lake
Karanji Lake
Kukkarahalli Lake
Lingambudhi Lake
Hebbal Lake

wikipedia.title: Mysore Race Course
wikipedia.text: Mysore Race Course is a racing track in Mysore city of Karnataka province, India.

wikipedia.title: Siddhartha Nagar
wikipedia.text: Siddhartha Nagar is an eastern suburb of Mysore city in Karnataka, a south Indian state.

wikipedia.title: Anjali Ashram, Mysore
wikipedia.text: Anjali Ashram is a Christian retreat in Mysore city in the Karnataka province of India.

wikipedia.title: Mysore Sand Sculpture Museum
wikipedia.text: Mysore Sand Sculpture Museum is the first sand sculpture museum in India, located in Mysore, Karnataka. It was inaugurated in 2014, with 150 sand sculptures on display, on a one-acre land at the base of Chamundi Hills. Each of the sculptures was created by sand artist MN Gowri and based on a theme such as Mysore's cultural heritage, wildlife and religion.

wikipedia.title: Abdul Nazir Sab State Institute of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj
wikipedia.text: The Abdul Nazir Sab State Institute of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj is a government institution located in Mysore, Karnataka. It was named after Abdul Nazir Sab, a former Karnataka Minister for Rural Development and Panchayat Raj, who was a strong advocate for the Panchayati Raj system and the decentralization of political power. The institute operates under the Department of Rural Development and Panchayat Raj (Karnataka) and provides training and capacity-building programs for elected representatives of Panchayat Raj institutions and officials from various development departments.

wikivoyage.title: Mysore
wikivoyage.text:
Mysore or Mysuru (ಮೈಸೂರು Maisūru) is the second-largest city of the Indian state of Karnataka after Bengaluru. It was the capital of the Wodeyar dynasty and is considered to be the cultural capital of Karnataka. Mysore is among the cleanest and best-planned cities in India. The regal city is striking a balance between olden times and modernity, resulting in the city being both old and new.


== See ==
1 Mysore Zoo (Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Gardens), Sri Chamarajendra Zoological Gardens, Zoo Main Road Indiranagar, ☏ +91 821 252 0302, zoomysore@gmail.com. Wed-Mon 8AM-5:30PM. The zoo was established under royal patronage in 1892, making it one of the oldest in the world. Mysore Zoo has had a successful breeding program and houses animals from more than 40 different countries, along with native Indian fauna, including Royal Bengal tigers, white tigers, elephants, fallow deer, Himalayan black bears, Gaur (Indian bison), white peafowl and African rhinos. The zoo is also home to many other exotic creatures from around the world, like Barbary sheep, giraffes, hippos and gorillas. The zoo encompasses Karanji Lake, which attracts several species of migratory birds during the breeding season, including painted storks, pelicans, and darters. Other attractions include the botanical garden with 35 species of exotic ornamental plants and 85 species of trees from India and abroad. Visitors can treat themselves to snacks and tender coconut that are available inside the zoo. Excellent mementoes are available in a souvenir shop. Vehicle parking is available in an open area opposite the zoo. The parking fee collected is ₹50 for buses, ₹30 for mini-buses or tempos, ₹10 for cars and ₹5 for two-wheelers. ₹40 for adults, ₹10 for children over 5, battery operated vehicle tour ₹100, ₹20 for camera and ₹50 for video camera (camcorder).  


=== Palaces ===

2 Mysore Palace. Definitely the number one attraction in Mysore. Intricately carved rosewood doors and ceilings, some with inlaid ivory work, marble figurines, collections of caskets, paintings of the members of the royal family and other objects of personal use exhibit such opulence, and over time have been preserved remarkably well. The guards quick out the public from the palace premises (gardens) around 18:00 to prepare for the 'light and sound' show in the evening. It starts at 19:00, lasts 40 minutes and is in Kannada language only, making it less interesting for foreigners, were it not for the impressive illumination of the whole palace at the end (19:40-45) with 100,000 bulbs. The ticket counter opens at 16:45 for the show (₹100). Entry is on the south side. You are required to leave your shoes outside before entering at a cost of ₹2 per pair. ₹100 for both Indian and foreign adults. (updated Oct 2024)
3 Cheluvamba Mansion.  (updated Apr 2026)
4 Chittaranjan Palace.  (updated Apr 2026)
5 Jayalakshmi Vilas, Manasagangotri. Fri-Mon 10AM-5PM. It was built by Maharani Regent Vani Vilasa Sannidhana, wife of Chamaraja Wodeyar, for her daughter Jayalakshami. It has around 200 rooms, an exotic dancing hall and a Kalyanmantap with intricately carved wood pillars. It was converted into a museum and stores artefacts about local folk and performing arts, tools and objects of various artisans and other archaeological findings. Princess Jayalakshmi was married to her maternal uncle. Dewan Sir M. Kantha Raja Urs. After independence, their son-in-law, Sirdar K. Basavaraj Urs, sold the property to the University of Mysore to start its postgraduate centre, and the then Vice Chancellor, Dr K.V. Puttapa christened the place as Manasa Gangothri. (updated Apr 2026)
6 Lalitha Mahal Palace, Lalitha Mahal Palace Rd, ☏ +91 80-40554055, info@junglelodges.com. Another palace that has been turned into a five-star hotel. It served as a royal summer residence for the Viceroy of India in the late 19th and early 19th century. You feel the antique-style grandeur and regality when you stay here. Guests should visit the hotel during the afternoon since it serves a great British high tea. It is situated close to the Chamundi Hills. 


=== Chamundi Hill ===

7 Chamundeshwari Temple, Chamundi Hill Road (at the top of Chamundi Hills), ☏ +91 821-259-0027. A beautiful temple of Goddess Chamundeshwari (or Chamundi Devi) with marvellous architecture. Wheelchair access is available. AC Volvo buses go up to Chamundi Hill and back from the city bus stand every twenty minutes (Nr. 201, ₹20). If you want to take the steps (and snap a picture at the Chumandi Hill viewpoint), take either 203, 205 or 401A (₹10) and get off at JSS College, from where you walk 800 m to the bottom of the stairs. ₹30 regular entry, ₹100 VIP (no queue). (updated Oct 2024)
 Jwalamukhi Tiruparasundari Temple (Chamundi Sister Temple), Uttanahalli, Off Nanjangud Road (MCTD 203 from City bus stand). One of the old temples of Mysore, Jwalamukhi Tirupparasunadri, is also an incarnation of Goddess Parasakthi, the creator. As per legend, the demon Mahisasura had a boon that if anyone killed him and blood spilt on the ground, each drop of blood would create a Mahisasura. Hence, during the process of slaying the demon, Goddess Chamundi consulted the help of Devi Tripura Sundari, who ensured that the blood drops did not touch the ground, by drinking every single drop of the blood falling out. Thus, the demon was destroyed. The Goddess stayed on the foothills of the hills, ensuring protection to all the devotees around the town. (updated Feb 2018)
8 Lookout View Point, Chamundi Hill (on the road that goes up the hill). The lookout provides an aerial view of Mysore, allowing you to see the entire white city and surrounding forest in all its glory. There are a few binoculars at the lookout point, though you would need to pay to use them. (updated Dec 2018)
9 Rajendra Vilas.  (updated Apr 2026)


=== Museums ===

10 Folklore Museum. closed Sun. Founded in 1968 and located in the University of Mysore campus, the museum has over 6500 folk art and folklore articles on display and exhibits arts and crafts from all over the state of Karnataka. It is housed in Jayalakhmi Mansion situated at Manasa Gangotri. The museum has detailed exhibits of "Yakshagana" and "Puppet art". (updated Apr 2026)
11 Jaganmohan Palace and Art Gallery (opposite City Bus Stand, Jagan Mohan Palace Road, Chamrajpura), ☏ +91 821 242 3693. daily 8:30AM-5:30PM. A former palace that has been converted into an art gallery and function hall. The palace for some time was home to the Wodeyar dynasty. The art gallery features paintings of many styles, including Mughlai, Mysorean and European. The most prominent works are those of Raja Ravi Varma, which are over 100 years old. A big part of the exhibition is comprised of very similar portraits of members of the Royal family. ₹60. (updated Apr 2026)
12 Kalashree Seashell Museum. A museum with sculptures made of seashell and conch by Radha Mallappa, including the sculptures of Ganesha, Shiva, the Taj Mahal and St. Philomena's Church. (updated Apr 2026)
13 Melody World Wax Museum, 1, Vihara Marga, Siddhartha Layout (near GST Bhavan), ☏ +91 8217624257, waxworldindia@gmail.com. Daily 9:30AM-7PM. Established in October 2010, this unique wax museum is based on musicians and musical instruments from all over the World. Exhibits a collection of over 100 life-size wax statues and over 1,500 types of musical instruments. ₹50. (updated Jun 2021)
14 Mysore Sand Sculpture Museum. 150 sand sculptures on display. It is not worth visiting unless it is on your way to another location. (updated Apr 2026)
15 Oriental Research Institute. Formerly known as the oriental library, it was started in 1891 and contains over 33,000 palm leaf manuscripts. 
16 Payana Museum.  (updated Apr 2026)
17 Railway Museum (near the back gate of the railway station). Exhibits vintage locomotives as they were in use. The second of such museums was set up after the Rail Museum in Delhi. The major attraction of the museum is the wagon used by the Queen of Mysore. There is a small toy train. The museum is a small one and can be visited while arriving or leaving Mysore during working hours. (updated Apr 2026)
18 Regional Museum of Natural History (near Nandhini Milk Dairy, back side of Postal Training Centre), ☏ +91 821 244 7046. 10AM-5PM (closed Mon). Has exhibits on plants, animals, and geology of the southern region of India. They conduct a show at intervals. They also have a cute watch tower for bird watching. The museum is situated in a beautiful garden. You can even visit the place just sit to in the gardens in the lush green surroundings. This facility is run by the central government of India. Free. (updated Apr 2026)


=== Religious sites ===

19 Datta Peetham (Sri Ganapati Sachchidananda Avadhoota Datta Peetham). An ashram in Mysore. It has beautiful gardens with bonsais among other plants. You can buy some herbal tea for an infusion, grown in the gardens.
